title: Perfect state transfer under matrix powers: parity and spectral arithmetic
abstract: For a real symmetric matrix $H$ and distinct vertices $a,b$, we classify exponents $k$ for which $H^k$ has perfect state transfer (PST) from $a$ to $b$. If their supported eigenvalues are integer multiples of a common positive number, every odd exponent reduces to $H$ and every positive even exponent reduces to $H^2$. We determine the minimum transfer times using a greatest common divisor of supported spectral differences. For rational symmetric matrices, symmetry of the source vertex support about zero implies the odd-power equivalence without a commensurability assumption; this includes all bipartite graphs. If the source vertex supports zero, PST under one positive even power implies PST under every positive even power. For a symmetric three-point quadratic spectrum whose outer projection signs agree and differ from the central sign, a nonzero rational shift leaves exactly one PST exponent. We classify all adjacency powers of hypercubes, cycles, and Johnson graphs, and all adjacency squares of paths. In particular, the adjacency matrix of $P_7$ has PST from vertex $2$ to vertex $6$ only at exponent $2$.
summary: This paper provides a rigorous mathematical classification of when Perfect State Transfer (PST) occurs for powers of a matrix $H$, often the adjacency matrix of a graph. It establishes that PST existence frequently follows a parity rule based on the spectral properties of $H$. The methodology combines spectral theory with number theory to precisely determine the allowed exponents $k$ for quantum state transfer.
main_problem: The paper classifies the exponents $k$ for which a real symmetric matrix $H$ (often an adjacency matrix) has Perfect State Transfer (PST) between two distinct vertices $a$ and $b$ when considering the matrix power $H^k$. It analyzes the interplay between spectral properties and arithmetic phase conditions governing this transfer.
main_result: The existence of PST often follows a parity rule: if the spectral supports are commensurable, PST occurs if $k$ is odd (related to $H$) or if $k$ is even (related to $H^2$). Specific graph families like hypercubes and paths are classified, showing PST is highly constrained.
method:
The analysis relies heavily on spectral theory, using spectral decomposition, spectral idempotents, and number-theoretic tools like the greatest common divisor (gcd) and 2-adic valuations ($
u_2$) to analyze phase compatibility conditions.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by a real symmetric matrix $H$, typically the adjacency matrix $A(G)$ of a graph $G$. The dynamics are governed by the evolution operator $\exp(-itH^k)$, where $H^k$ is the $k$-th power of the matrix.
key_observables: Perfect State Transfer (PST) existence, minimum transfer time (related to $	ext{gcd}$ of spectral differences), and the parity of the exponent $k$.
important_parameters: The structure of the graph $G$ (e.g., path $P_7$, hypercubes), the vertex pair $(a, b)$, and the spectral properties of $H$.
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes that the supported eigenvalues are integer multiples of a common positive number ($c\mathbb{Z}$) or that the matrix is rational symmetric.
paper_structure: The paper develops from general functional calculus criteria to specific theorems establishing parity dichotomies (Theorem 1.1) for PST exponents, followed by specialized analyses for rational matrices and detailed classifications for specific graph families like paths and Johnson graphs.
why_interesting: This work provides deep mathematical tools for analyzing quantum walks and quantum information transfer on graphs, which is highly relevant to quantum network theory and quantum computation models.
